U-08 Report an issue and support chat

Bangla name: ইস্যু রিপোর্ট ও সাপোর্ট চ্যাট

← 30 · User app · Contents · Open queries

1. Name and purpose

Report an issue and support chat. The customer raises a problem against one of their orders and then talks to support about it. The rules are the server's: one issue per order and 600 characters per description. The app is the counterpart of P-12; the server-side findings in that entry — the unauthenticated chat REST API, the missing unique index, the size-limit mismatch — apply here unchanged.

2. Trigger and actor

Signed-in customer. Routes /issues (list), /reportIssue (raise), /chatCommunication (thread).

3. Business flow

  1. From My bookings the customer opens Report issue for an order.
  2. They write up to 600 characters, optionally attach a file, and submit; the description becomes the first chat message.
  3. The customer sees their issue list with its status (Open or Resolved).
  4. In the thread they send text, see replies, typing indicators and attachments, and download any attachment.

4. Technical flow

  1. [HTTP + user token] POST userissue/api/v1/user-issue with CreateReportIssue { publicOrderId, programId, description } — the same DTO as the portal (P-12 §6). The 600-character limit and the one-issue-per-order rule are enforced in ReportIssueManager, not by a database constraint (Q-47).
  2. [HTTP + user token] GET userissue/api/v1/user-issue/user/{userId} — the list; GET userissue/api/v1/user-issue/user-detail/{publicOrderId} — one issue.
  3. [HTTP + user token] GET userissue/api/v1/user-issue-chat/$issueId/messages — chat history, via ChatApiService.getMessages(issueId: …).
  4. Sending is SignalR-first with REST fallback (chat_communication_repository_impl.dart:32-36): dart try { await signalRService.sendMessage(chatModel.toJson()); } catch (e) { await chatApiService.sendMessage(issueId: issueId, chatModel: chatModel); } So the app is not REST-only: it holds a live SignalR connection (signal_r_service.dart, startConnection(issueId, onNewMessage: …) / stopConnection()), and falls back to POST userissue/api/v1/user-issue-chat/send only when the hub call throws. This corrects the assumption recorded in the plan that the app's chat is REST-only.
  5. [HTTP, no auth] → chat REST POST userissue/api/v1/user-issue-chat/send and GET userissue/api/v1/user-issue-chat/message/$messageId/attachment/download. [UNCONFIRMED: Q-46] — the fallback path is the unauthenticated chat API whose senderId/senderType are client-supplied (P-12 note 1), so the app's fallback path is the exposed one.
  6. Attachments are uploaded as multipart and downloaded through DownloadService.downloadFile(url: await chatApiService.getUrl(messageId: …), headers: await chatApiService.getAttachmentHeaders(), …, saveInPublicStorage: true, …) (:41-58), then opened with openFile.
  7. The 600-character limit is mirrored client-side, but the file-size limit differs from the server's 10 MB (Q-48) [UNCONFIRMED: Q-48].

Method Path Auth Notes

GET /userissue/api/v1/user-issue/user/{userId} User issue list
GET /userissue/api/v1/user-issue/user-detail/{publicOrderId} User one issue

GET /userissue/api/v1/user-issue-chat/message/$messageId/attachment/download none attachment download

7. Data and side effects

UserIssues row, chat message rows, an S3 object per attachment, and a SignalR group membership — identical to the portal (P-12 §7).

9. Handover notes

  1. The app's chat is SignalR-first, not REST-only (§4 note 4). The plan's earlier assumption is corrected here; the portal is SignalR-only and the app adds the REST fallback.
  2. The REST fallback is the unauthenticated endpoint (Q-46). A customer on a flaky connection at an event — exactly when support matters most — silently downgrades to the anonymous API.
  3. A failed hub send is swallowed into the fallback, so a genuine send error surfaces as a REST error and the original SignalR cause is lost (catch (e) with an unused e).
  4. Attachment download also uses the anonymous endpoint, and writes into public storage (saveInPublicStorage: true), which means any app on the device can read support attachments.
  5. No read receipts from the app — the unread-count endpoints exist on the server but the app does not call them, so a badge count cannot be shown.
  6. Issue-resolved push is not implemented server-side (Q-50), so the app will not notify the customer when support answers.
